---
title: "Step 4. Upload the test set and run the AI"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

Put the same images into every benchmark project, one deployment per class, and
start the AI.

## What the step does

For each run project in the config:

1. Checks the project name matches the config (never writes to any other project).
2. Creates a location and a camera called `benchmark`, resolves one tag per class
   (`tags/resolve`), and creates one deployment per class carrying that tag. Dates
   span 2015 to 2026 so every image timestamp falls inside the deployment.
3. Streams the images: each batch of 10 is downloaded from its source project,
   uploaded to every run that still needs it, then deleted. Peak disk use stays
   at a few hundred MB.
4. When a class is complete in a run, sets `automaticAi: true` and calls
   `finalizeUpload`; WIMP creates sequences and queues the AI.

```{python eval=FALSE}
import subprocess
# time-boxed and resumable: exit code 75 means "run again"
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "upload", "--config", "config/awt_2026_11.yaml",
                "--max-seconds", "900"])
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "status", "--config", "config/awt_2026_11.yaml"])
```

## Timing (AWT, 3 Nov 2026)

4,399 images x 5 projects = 21,995 uploads, streamed from the cloud workspace with
12 parallel batches in about 85 minutes (about 55 source images a minute, each going
to five projects; peak local disk use under 200 MB). WIMP answered 5 batches with
`500 Unexpected error during upload`; each was retried on the next pass and every
deployment ended with exactly the manifest count (checked with `status`). The AI
keeps pace on PROD; TEST queues deployments and finishes later. A pilot class
(Wallabia bicolor, 60 images) reached AI processing within a minute of finalizing.

## Known issues

- With a 0-second sequence cut-off, images with identical timestamps (camera
  bursts within one second) still form one sequence: 60 pilot images made 58
  sequences. Event-level scoring gives such images the same prediction, which is
  what a WIMP user sees.
- The API cannot delete deployments. A failed class is re-uploaded into its
  existing deployment (the state file records each file per run).
